Fig. 3: Performance analysis of the proposed controller with Dynamics Reward. The plots demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains primary task performance while significantly improving auxiliary metrics related to efficiency and smoothness.

Fig. 2: Complete architecture diagram depicting the baseline controller with integrated Intrinsic Dynamics Head. The ID Head processes state information as input and generates torque predictions, which in turn are used to compute the Dynamics Reward and Auxiliary Loss.

Fig. 4: Real robot performance comparison between baseline and dynamics reward policies with identical velocity commands (b). The dynamics reward policy demonstrates improved performance in joint position error rates (c), lower torque requirements (d), and reduced power consumption (e), validating the simulation results in real-world conditions.

TABLE VI: Performance Metrics Comparison on Real Robot. Metrics were computed over 10,000 policy steps of real robot data, averaged across 2 independent runs for each configuration. Bold values indicate best performance, underlined values indicate second-best performance, and arrows (↑/↓) indicate whether higher or lower values are better.
